observed_then.error: NoBibliographySectionError: No bibliography/references heading found in the document.

cases.note: Two defenses contradicted each other: find_bibliography_section takes the first 'References' so a repeated running header cannot move the section start, but _drop_repeated_isolated_lines ran first and deleted every copy including the real heading, so there was no section left to find.

cases.variant: Bulleted bibliography, entry split across a wrap/page break into two bullets
cases.round: parser diagnostic on Siepe et al. 2024
cases.note: pymupdf4llm renders a bulleted bibliography as one list item per entry, but a wrap or page break falling mid-entry can make it emit the continuation as its own separate bullet: once with a dangling hyphen wrap, once where the break falls right after a title-ending period (indistinguishable from a finished entry by punctuation alone) with a page-number/running-header pair sitting between the two bullets in the source PDF (already stripped by the earlier normalize passes by the time this one runs). Neither continuation carries its own author-start marker or year, unlike a real next entry.
cases.text:
References

- Doe, J. (2020). A title that wraps across a break in the middle of a –

- word. Journal of Examples, 1(1), 1-10.

- Roe, R. (2021). A second reference ending in a normal sentence.

- Continuing without its own author or year. Journal of Methods, 3(2), 100-120. https://doi.org/10.1234/example

- Young, Y. (2022). A third, real entry. Journal of Cases, 4(1), 1-5.

cases.variant: Bulleted bibliography, many-author entry split across a wrap/page break right before its last author's 'and Surname, I.'
cases.round: parser diagnostic on a user-supplied preprint
cases.note: APA_AUTHOR_START_RE's optional particle prefix (added for 'van der Veen, D.'-style surnames) also matches the literal conjunction 'and' introducing a wrapped list's last author ('and Young, Y.'), so the merge heuristic's has_own_evidence check mistook the continuation bullet for a genuine new entry and refused to merge it back, even though it also carried its own DOI (continuation evidence).
